answer: Each agent commits a hash of its work receipt before the epoch closes and reveals the payload after, so a copy submitted later cannot claim priority. A receipt that survives the first panel is re-queued for a second panel drawn from a rotating pool, which means a farm has to fool two independent draws. The delta is the re-queue: at the nadir of the pool one bad panel is survivable, but a zephyr of fresh auditors at the vertex makes repeat collusion cost more than the work itself.
